function.en: Takes colour pictures of the ground in daylight.
function.zh-TW: 白天拍地面的彩色照片

explainer.en: A small digital camera like the one in your phone, but pointed at Earth. It only works in daylight, because it needs sunlight bouncing off the ground. Swarms of shoebox-sized satellites carry cameras like this to photograph the whole planet every day.
explainer.zh-TW: 跟手機相機同一個原理，只是鏡頭朝著地球。它靠地面反射的陽光，所以只能白天拍。有些公司放了一大群鞋盒大小的衛星，每天把整個地球拍一遍。

description.en: A shoebox-sized colour camera, about 6-7 m per pixel from 700 km. Light and cheap, but it only works in daylight and sees no more than your eyes do.
description.zh-TW: 鞋盒大小的彩色相機，從 700 公里高拍，每個像素約 6–7 公尺。輕又便宜，但只能在白天拍，看到的和肉眼差不多。

source.title: SatCatalog: Simera Sense TriScape100; Sensors 2023, 23(13):6192
source.note: sourced: 1.1 kg, 6.0 W average; GSD 4.75 m at 500 km (sister model MultiScape100). derived: 6.65 m at 700 km (GSD scales with altitude; all imager resolutions in this file are quoted at 700 km so they compare fairly), 33 GB/day = 61 Mbit/s x 72 min of imaging per day (5% duty cycle is an estimate). estimate: cost

function.en: Sees several colours of light, including near-infrared, to tell crops, water and soil apart.
function.zh-TW: 分好幾種顏色的光拍照，分得出作物、水和土壤

explainer.en: Instead of one colour photo, it takes several pictures at once through different filters, including near-infrared light our eyes cannot see. Healthy plants reflect near-infrared strongly, so farmers and foresters use it to spot crops in trouble. The Landsat satellites have done this for half a century.
explainer.zh-TW: 它隔著不同的濾鏡同時拍好幾張，其中一張是眼睛看不到的近紅外光。健康的植物很會反射近紅外光，農業和林業單位就靠這點找出生病的作物。Landsat 衛星拍這個已經拍了半個世紀。

description.en: Seven colour bands from visible to near-infrared, about 2 m pixels from 700 km. Tells healthy crops from stressed ones and water from mud. Daylight only.
description.zh-TW: 從可見光到近紅外線共 7 個波段，從 700 公里高拍像素約 2 公尺。分得出健康和缺水的作物、清水和泥水。只能白天拍。

source.title: SatCatalog: Simera Sense MultiScape200 CIS
source.note: sourced: 12.1 kg dry, 5.8 W imaging, 7 VNIR bands, GSD 1.5 at 500 km. derived: 2.1 m at 700 km. estimate: ~41 GB/day (10 km swath and 150 s of imaging per day assumed), cost

function.en: Sees heat: finds fires and hot spots, day or night.
function.zh-TW: 看得到熱：日夜都能找出火災和高溫點

explainer.en: Everything warm glows in long-wave infrared, even at night. This camera measures that glow to read the temperature of the ground: fires, volcanoes, hot cities, cool lakes. Its detector must be kept very cold by a small refrigerator called a cryocooler, otherwise the camera would see its own heat.
explainer.zh-TW: 有溫度的東西都會發出長波紅外線，晚上也一樣。這台相機量的就是這種光，讀得出火災、火山、城市和湖面的溫度。感測器要靠一台叫製冷機的小冰箱降溫，不然相機會看到自己的熱。

description.en: Sees heat instead of light, so it works at night: wildfires, volcanoes, city heat islands. Its cryocooler draws steady power.
description.zh-TW: 看的是熱而不是光，所以晚上也能用：野火、火山、城市熱島。製冷機需要穩定供電。

source.title: NASA NTRS: Jhabvala et al., CTI-2 (Compact Thermal Imager 2), Table 4
source.note: sourced: mass 8 kg, cryocooler 12 W, 8.4 Mbit/s, 37 m from 410 km = 63 m from 700 km. derived: 23 GB/day at a 25% duty cycle (estimate). estimate: 25 W total power, cost

function.en: Splits light into hundreds of colours to identify materials.
function.zh-TW: 把光分成上百種顏色，辨認地面是什麼物質

explainer.en: It splits light into hundreds of narrow colours, like a prism. Every material, from minerals to plastic to algae, leaves its own fingerprint in that rainbow, so scientists can tell what the ground is made of. The price is a flood of data.
explainer.zh-TW: 它像稜鏡一樣把光拆成上百種很窄的顏色。礦物、塑膠、藻類在這些顏色裡各有各的特徵，科學家看了就知道地面是什麼做的。代價是資料量很大。

description.en: 239 narrow bands: a full spectrum for every pixel (about 34 m from 700 km), enough to identify minerals and plant species. Heavy, power-hungry and full of data.
description.zh-TW: 239 個窄波段：每個像素（從 700 公里高約 34 公尺）都有完整光譜，能辨認礦物和植物種類。又重又耗電，資料量很大。

source.title: eoPortal: PRISMA (ASI)
source.note: sourced: instrument < 90 kg, < 110 W average, 30 m from 615 km, 66 VNIR + 173 SWIR bands, 200,000 km2 per day. derived: 34 m at 700 km, 80 GB/day (12-bit depth assumed). estimate: cost (PRISMA's is not published), development time

function.en: A radar that images the ground through clouds and darkness.
function.zh-TW: 穿過雲層和黑夜拍地面的雷達

explainer.en: A radar that sends out its own microwave pulses and listens for the echo. Because it brings its own 'light', it sees through clouds, smoke and darkness. By combining echoes along its path it builds a sharp image, as if it had a giant antenna. Used to map floods, ice and earthquakes.
explainer.zh-TW: 這種雷達自己發出微波脈衝，再聽回波。「光源」自己帶，所以雲、煙和黑夜都擋不住它。把沿路收到的回波拼起來，效果就像一根巨大的天線，影像因此很清楚。常用來測繪洪水、冰層和地震。

description.en: Brings its own light: radar pulses see through clouds, smoke and night, 3 m strips. Floods and hurricanes are usually cloudy, so this is the instrument that still works.
description.zh-TW: 自己帶光源：雷達脈衝可以穿透雲、煙和黑夜，條帶解析度 3 公尺。洪水和颱風時通常是陰天，這時只有它照樣能用。

source.title: eoPortal: ICEYE constellation
source.note: sourced: 85 kg spacecraft, 3.2 x 0.4 m antenna, 4 kW RF peak, stripmap 3 m, 140 Mbit/s downlink. estimate: instrument share 40 kg, 150 W orbit average (a few minutes of imaging per orbit), 34 GB/day, cost

function.en: Measures how much carbon dioxide is in the air below.
function.zh-TW: 量測下方空氣裡的二氧化碳有多少

explainer.en: Sunlight passing through the air loses a little of certain colours that carbon dioxide absorbs. This spectrometer measures exactly how much is missing, and from that works out how much carbon dioxide is in the column of air below. NASA's Orbiting Carbon Observatory missions map the whole planet this way.
explainer.zh-TW: 陽光穿過大氣時，有幾種特定的顏色會被二氧化碳吸收。這台光譜儀量出少了多少，就能推算下方整柱空氣裡有多少二氧化碳。NASA 的軌道碳觀測衛星就是這樣畫出全球的二氧化碳地圖。

description.en: Three high-resolution spectrometers that measure carbon dioxide from sunlight reflected off the surface, the instrument built for NASA's Orbiting Carbon Observatory.
description.zh-TW: 三台高解析度光譜儀，從地表反射的陽光量二氧化碳濃度。原本是為 NASA 軌道碳觀測衛星（OCO）做的。

source.title: OCO launch press kit (NASA/JPL 2009); OCO Mishap Investigation summary
source.note: sourced: instrument 135 kg; footprint 1.29 x 2.25 km; daily return 6.75 min at 150 Mbit/s = 7.6 GB/day (derived). sourced: instrument power < 125 W (press kit; game uses 100 W). estimate: $110M so the spacecraft and instrument total about $209M (the loss figure in the mishap report, which appears to exclude the ~$70M Taurus XL launch). Adding the launch gives roughly the press kit's $273.4M total NASA investment used as the hist_oco budget

name.zh-TW: 機身貼片太陽能板（0.4 m²）

function.en: Solar cells stuck on the body: makes power in sunlight.
function.zh-TW: 貼在機身上的太陽能電池：有陽光就發電

explainer.en: Solar cells glued directly onto the outside of the spacecraft. Simple and sturdy, with nothing to unfold, but the body only has so much surface, and some sides always face away from the Sun.
explainer.zh-TW: 直接黏在衛星外殼上的太陽能電池。簡單又耐用，沒有東西要展開；但機身的表面就那麼大，而且總有幾面背對太陽。

description.en: Cells glued straight onto the bus. Nothing to deploy, nothing to break, but little area.
description.zh-TW: 電池片直接貼在機身上。不用展開、不會卡住，但面積很小。

source.title: NASA SST State-of-the-Art, ch. 3 Power
source.note: estimate: ~3 kg/m2 for body-mounted panels; cost ~400 USD/W

function.en: Fold-out solar wings: more power in sunlight.
function.zh-TW: 展開式太陽能翼：日照時發更多電

explainer.en: Panels folded flat against the spacecraft for launch, then swung open once in orbit. Opening them is one of the tensest moments after launch: if a hinge sticks, the mission may not have enough power.
explainer.zh-TW: 發射時折起來貼著機身，入軌後才打開。這是發射後最讓人緊張的時刻之一：鉸鏈一卡住，電可能就不夠用。

description.en: Two hinged wings that unfold after launch. Three times the area, at the cost of mass and a deployment that has to work.
description.zh-TW: 發射後才展開的兩片鉸鏈翼。面積是三倍，但比較重，而且展開必須成功。

source.title: NASA SST State-of-the-Art, ch. 3 Power, Table 3-2
source.note: derived: 6 kg/m2 = 340 W/m2 / 53.6-60 W/kg (Lockheed Martin SmallSat Array, GomSpace TSP). estimate: cost ~400 USD/W

function.en: A big fold-out solar array for power-hungry spacecraft.
function.zh-TW: 大型展開太陽能陣列，給很耗電的太空船用

explainer.en: A big array of solar wings for power-hungry spacecraft, like the ones on large Earth-observation satellites. More area catches more sunlight, but it is heavier, wobbles more, and has more joints that must unfold perfectly.
explainer.zh-TW: 大型地球觀測衛星上那種大太陽能翼。面積越大接到的陽光越多，但也更重、更會晃，要順利打開的關節也更多。

description.en: About the size of OCO's array. Enough to run a big instrument through years of degradation.
description.zh-TW: 大約是 OCO 太陽能板的大小。即使衰退多年，也撐得起大型儀器。

source.title: OCO launch press kit (NASA/JPL 2009); NASA SST-SoA Table 3-2
source.note: sourced: OCO array 'total surface area of 3.88 square meters'. derived: 6 kg/m2. estimate: cost ~400 USD/W

function.en: Stores power for when the spacecraft is in Earth's shadow.
function.zh-TW: 儲存電力，衛星進到地球影子裡時用

explainer.en: Rechargeable lithium-ion cells, like a laptop battery built for space. A satellite in low orbit goes through Earth's shadow many times a day, so the battery is charged and drained over and over for years. Draining it deeply every time wears it out fast.
explainer.zh-TW: 可以充電的鋰電池，就像太空版的筆電電池。低軌道的衛星一天要穿過地球影子很多次，所以電池好幾年都在反覆充放電。每次都放得很深，電池就會很快耗損。

description.en: A CubeSat-class battery. Fine for a small load; a big load drains it deep every orbit and wears it out.
description.zh-TW: 立方衛星等級的電池。負載小沒問題；負載大時每圈都放得很深，很快就會耗損。

source.title: NASA SST State-of-the-Art, ch. 3 Power, Table 3-5
source.note: sourced: packs 141.8-178.1 Wh/kg (game 145). estimate: flight-qualified cost ~200 USD/Wh

function.en: Stores power for the shadow part of each orbit.
function.zh-TW: 儲存電力，給每一圈的地影時段用

explainer.en: A larger lithium-ion pack. A bigger battery only needs to give up a small share of its charge in each shadow, and shallow cycles let a battery survive tens of thousands of orbits.
explainer.zh-TW: 比較大的鋰電池組。電池越大，每次地影只用掉一小部分電量；放得淺，就能撐過好幾萬圈。

description.en: Enough for a microsatellite to ride through the shadow at shallow depth of discharge.
description.zh-TW: 足夠讓微衛星以較淺的放電深度撐過地球影子。

source.title: NASA SST State-of-the-Art, ch. 3 Power, Table 3-5
source.note: derived: 400 Wh / ~148 Wh/kg. estimate: cost ~200 USD/Wh

function.en: Stores a lot of power for long shadows and heavy loads.
function.zh-TW: 儲存大量電力，撐長時間地影和大負載

explainer.en: A heavy-duty battery for big loads and long shadows. The International Space Station swapped its old batteries for lithium-ion ones like this, carried up by spacewalking astronauts.
explainer.zh-TW: 給大負載和長地影用的重型電池。國際太空站就把舊電池換成了這類鋰電池，是太空人出艙一顆一顆換上去的。

description.en: A big pack for big loads or long shadows (GEO, lunar orbit).
description.zh-TW: 給大負載或長影子（地球同步、月球軌道）用的大電池組。

source.title: NASA SST State-of-the-Art, ch. 3 Power, Table 3-5
source.note: derived: 1,500 Wh / 150 Wh/kg. estimate: cost ~200 USD/Wh

name.zh-TW: S 波段低增益天線（10 Mbps）

function.en: Sends data back to the ground.
function.zh-TW: 把資料傳回地面

explainer.en: A small, flat radio antenna that talks to the ground in the S-band, the same family of frequencies as Wi-Fi and Bluetooth. It is robust and does not need to point precisely, but it sends data slowly.
explainer.zh-TW: 小小的平板天線，用 S 頻段和地面通訊，和 Wi-Fi、藍牙是同一類頻率。它很耐用，也不用對得很準，但傳資料比較慢。

description.en: Simple patch antennas that work at any attitude. Reliable, but slow: fine for telemetry, tight for imagery.
description.zh-TW: 任何姿態都能通訊的簡單貼片天線。可靠但慢：傳遙測沒問題，傳影像就很吃緊。

source.title: NASA SST State-of-the-Art, ch. 9 Communications, Table 9-3
source.note: sourced: S-band transmitters 1,000-20,000 kbps, 27-33 dBm, 70-250 g. estimate: 10 Mbit/s closed link, 8 W DC while transmitting (~25% PA efficiency), cost

function.en: Sends data back to the ground, faster.
function.zh-TW: 把資料傳回地面，比較快

explainer.en: A higher-frequency X-band radio. Higher frequencies can carry more data per second, which is why most Earth-observation satellites send their pictures down in X-band during each short pass over a ground station.
explainer.zh-TW: 頻率更高的 X 頻段無線電。頻率越高，每秒能載的資料越多，所以大多數地球觀測衛星都用 X 頻段，趁著每次短短的過站時間把照片傳下來。

description.en: The OCO set-up: an X-band transmitter and a body-mounted patch antenna, 15 times faster than S-band.
description.zh-TW: 和 OCO 一樣的配置：X 波段發射機加機身貼片天線，比 S 波段快 15 倍。

source.title: OCO launch press kit (NASA/JPL 2009); NASA SST-SoA Table 9-3
source.note: sourced: 'downlinked at a rate of 150 megabits per second through the X-band transmitter and a body-mounted X-band patch antenna'; X-band transmitters 0.27-2.4 kg. estimate: 25 W DC, cost

name.zh-TW: 高速 X 波段（1 Gbps）

function.en: Sends data back to the ground, very fast.
function.zh-TW: 把資料傳回地面，很快

explainer.en: A fast X-band radio with a focused antenna. It squeezes far more data into each pass, but it draws a lot of power while transmitting and must be aimed at the ground station.
explainer.zh-TW: 高速的 X 頻段無線電，配上聚焦的天線。每次過站能傳的資料多很多，但發送時很耗電，而且要對準地面站。

description.en: A modern high-rate downlink of the kind Planet flies. Moves tens of gigabytes in a single pass, but draws 50 W while it talks.
description.zh-TW: Planet 衛星用的那種新一代高速下傳。一次過境就能傳幾十 GB，但傳輸時耗電 50 W。

source.title: eoPortal: Planet (HSD2 radio)
source.note: sourced: 1,674 Mbit/s maximum achieved on orbit, 50 W during downlink. estimate: 1 Gbit/s sustained average, mass, cost

description.en: One high-latitude antenna rented by the minute. Long gaps between contacts mean data waits on board.
description.zh-TW: 按分鐘租用一座高緯度天線。兩次通聯間隔很長，資料要在衛星上排隊等。

source.title: AWS Ground Station pricing (AWS Price List API, 2026-09-11)
source.note: sourced: wideband on-demand $22/min (Ohio, Oregon). derived: 11 passes x 8 min x 365 days x $22 = $0.71M/yr (11 passes/day: the same high-latitude station assumption as orbits.json)

description.en: Three stations spread in longitude: three times the contact time and much shorter waits.
description.zh-TW: 經度分散的三座站：通聯時間三倍，等待時間短很多。

source.title: AWS Ground Station pricing (AWS Price List API, 2026-09-11)
source.note: derived: 3 x $0.71M/yr

description.en: A global network including a polar site that sees a polar orbiter on nearly every revolution.
description.zh-TW: 包含極區站的全球網路，極軌衛星幾乎每一圈都看得到。

source.title: AWS Ground Station pricing; Wikipedia: Svalbard Satellite Station
source.note: sourced: SvalSat sees low polar orbiters on every revolution. derived: 6 x $0.71M/yr

function.en: The spacecraft's brain: runs it and stores data between ground passes.
function.zh-TW: 衛星的大腦：控制衛星、在兩次通聯之間儲存資料

explainer.en: The spacecraft's brain: a small computer that runs the satellite, follows commands from the ground and stores the data until the next pass. Built from ordinary electronics, so it is cheap but has little storage and little protection against radiation.
explainer.zh-TW: 衛星的大腦：一台小電腦，負責控制衛星、執行地面的指令，並把資料存到下一次過站。用的是一般的電子零件，便宜，但儲存空間小，也不太耐輻射。

description.en: A commercial off-the-shelf board. Tiny, cheap, little storage, and only modest radiation tolerance.
description.zh-TW: 商用現成電路板。小又便宜，儲存空間少，抗輻射能力普通。

source.title: NASA SST State-of-the-Art, ch. 8 Avionics, Table 8-4
source.note: sourced: EnduroSat OBC 1.5 W peak; Kryten-M3 20 krad; onboard memory 'hundreds of KB to several GB'. estimate: mass, 8 GB

name.zh-TW: 電腦 + 大容量記憶體（128 GB）

function.en: The spacecraft's brain with a large data store.
function.zh-TW: 衛星的大腦，附大容量資料儲存

explainer.en: A flight computer with a large solid-state recorder, like a big memory card. When the satellite collects more data than it can send in one pass, the rest waits here. If the recorder fills up, new data has nowhere to go.
explainer.zh-TW: 附有大容量固態記錄器的飛行電腦，像一張大記憶卡。衛星收集的資料一次過站傳不完，剩下的就在這裡排隊。記錄器滿了，新資料就沒地方放。

description.en: An FPGA computer with a large recorder. Holds many orbits of imagery, still commercial-grade against radiation.
description.zh-TW: FPGA 電腦加大容量記錄器。能存好幾圈的影像，抗輻射仍是商用等級。

source.title: NASA SST-SoA Table 8-4 (Aerospacelab OBC); SatCatalog MultiScape200
source.note: sourced: < 4 W, 1.325 kg; 128 GB internal storage (MultiScape200); COTS 20-40 krad (Bradford 30 krad). estimate: cost

function.en: A radiation-tough, doubled-up spacecraft brain.
function.zh-TW: 抗輻射、雙套備援的衛星大腦

explainer.en: A radiation-hardened computer, with a second copy ready to take over. Energetic particles in space can flip bits or destroy chips; parts built to resist them are slower and expensive, which is why Mars rovers use processors that look old-fashioned.
explainer.zh-TW: 抗輻射的電腦，還有一套備援隨時可以接手。太空中的高能粒子會翻轉記憶體裡的位元、甚至打壞晶片；能抵抗的零件比較慢也比較貴，所以火星車用的處理器看起來都很老派。

description.en: Two radiation-hardened computers with a solid-state recorder. Survives GEO radiation and fails over automatically, but it is heavy and expensive.
description.zh-TW: 兩台抗輻射電腦加固態記錄器。撐得過地球同步軌道的輻射，壞一台會自動切換，但又重又貴。

source.title: NASA SST-SoA Table 8-4 (Aitech SP0-S); OCO launch press kit
source.note: sourced: 100 krad TID, 12 W; OCO used a RAD6000 with a 96-gigabit recorder. estimate: dual-string mass, 64 GB, cost

function.en: Keeps the spacecraft pointed the right way.
function.zh-TW: 讓衛星維持正確的指向

explainer.en: A tiny attitude-control unit: sensors that find the Sun, stars and Earth's magnetic field, plus small wheels and magnets to turn the spacecraft. Enough to keep a small satellite pointed in roughly the right direction.
explainer.zh-TW: 小型的姿態控制模組：用感測器找太陽、星星和地球磁場，再用小飛輪和磁力棒轉動衛星。足夠讓小衛星大致對準正確的方向。

description.en: An all-in-one unit with three tiny reaction wheels and a star tracker. Accurate, but there is no spare wheel.
description.zh-TW: 三顆小反應輪加星象儀的一體式模組。很準，但沒有備用反應輪。

source.title: NASA SST State-of-the-Art, ch. 5 GNC, Table 5-2 (BCT XACT-50)
source.note: sourced: 1.230 kg, 0.003/0.007 deg. estimate: 4 W, cost, reliability

function.en: Spinning wheels and a star camera that point the spacecraft steadily.
function.zh-TW: 用旋轉的飛輪和星象儀穩定指向

explainer.en: Reaction wheels are heavy flywheels: spin one faster and the spacecraft turns the other way, without using any fuel. Paired with a star camera that recognises constellations, they hold the satellite very steady.
explainer.zh-TW: 反應輪是很重的飛輪：讓它轉快一點，衛星就往反方向轉，一滴燃料都不用。再配一台會認星座的星象儀，衛星就能指得很穩。

description.en: Three wheels are needed to point; the fourth is a spare. Kepler lost two of four and nearly ended its mission.
description.zh-TW: 指向需要三顆輪子，第四顆是備用。克卜勒太空望遠鏡四顆壞了兩顆，任務差點結束。

source.title: NASA SST State-of-the-Art, ch. 5 GNC, Table 5-3 (BCT RW8)
source.note: sourced: RW8 4.4 kg, 8 Nms. derived: 4 x 4.4 kg + ~2 kg of sensors. estimate: 30 W average, cost

name.zh-TW: 高精度姿態控制（4 顆大反應輪）

function.en: Very steady, very precise pointing.
function.zh-TW: 最穩、最準的指向控制

explainer.en: Large reaction wheels and precise star trackers for the steadiest pointing, the kind space telescopes need. The Hubble Space Telescope can hold its aim as steadily as keeping a laser on a coin many kilometres away.
explainer.zh-TW: 大型反應輪加上精密的星象儀，提供最穩的指向，太空望遠鏡就需要這種。哈伯太空望遠鏡能把指向穩定到像是在好幾公里外把雷射光點固定在一枚硬幣上。

description.en: Big wheels for a big spacecraft and arc-second pointing, with a spare. Heavy and power-hungry.
description.zh-TW: 大衛星用的大反應輪，指向精度到角秒，含備用。又重又耗電。

source.title: NASA SST State-of-the-Art, ch. 5 GNC (BCT RW16, Flexcore)
source.note: sourced: RW16 7.5 kg, 16 Nms; Flexcore 0.002 deg. derived: 4 x 7.5 kg + sensors. estimate: 50 W average, cost

function.en: A cover plate: no engine, no fuel.
function.zh-TW: 封板：不裝引擎，也沒有燃料

explainer.en: No engine at all. Even very high up there is a whisper of air that slowly drags a satellite down; without an engine, the orbit's natural lifetime decides how long the mission can last.
explainer.zh-TW: 不裝引擎。就算飛得很高，還是有一點點空氣會慢慢把衛星往下拖；沒有引擎，任務能撐多久就看軌道自己掉得多快。

description.en: Saves mass and money. The orbit is whatever the rocket gave you, and drag decides how long you stay.
description.zh-TW: 省質量也省錢。軌道就是火箭給的那個，能待多久由大氣阻力決定。

source.title: Design option
source.note: no propulsion: lifetime limited by natural orbit decay

function.en: A small engine and fuel tank to keep the orbit up.
function.zh-TW: 小型引擎和燃料箱，用來維持軌道高度

explainer.en: A small thruster burning a 'green' propellant that is much less toxic than traditional rocket fuel, so it is safer to load on the ground. Short burns now and then lift the orbit back up against air drag.
explainer.zh-TW: 小型推進器，燒的是比傳統火箭燃料毒性低很多的「綠色」推進劑，在地面加注比較安全。偶爾點火一下，就能把被空氣拖低的軌道推回去。

description.en: A small non-toxic propulsion module, as flown on SkySat. About 150 m/s for a microsatellite.
description.zh-TW: SkySat 用的小型低毒推進模組。微衛星大約可以有 150 m/s 的速度變化量。

source.title: NASA SST State-of-the-Art, ch. 4 Propulsion, Table 4-3 (ECAPS SkySat 1N HPGP)
source.note: sourced: 22 kg wet, 21 kN*s total impulse, > 200 s; green monoprop 231-255 s. derived: propellant 21,000/(220 x 9.81) = 9.7 kg so the game's Isp reproduces the sourced total impulse; dry 11.3 kg (game wet mass 21.0 kg; the remaining ~1 kg of the sourced 22 kg is unusable residual propellant, not modelled). estimate: Isp 220 s average, 3 W heaters, cost

function.en: A bigger engine and fuel tank to keep the orbit up for longer.
function.zh-TW: 較大的引擎和燃料箱，可以維持軌道更久

explainer.en: Hydrazine thrusters: the classic spacecraft engine. The propellant flows over a hot catalyst and decomposes into hot gas, with no igniter needed. Reliable and proven on decades of missions, but toxic to handle.
explainer.zh-TW: 聯氨推進器，衛星最經典的引擎。推進劑流過高溫的觸媒就會分解成高溫氣體，不需要點火。幾十年的任務證明它很可靠，但處理起來有毒。

description.en: A classic hydrazine tank and thrusters with OCO's propellant load: years of drag make-up or station keeping.
description.zh-TW: 經典的聯氨貯箱加推進器，推進劑量和 OCO 一樣：足夠多年的阻力補償或軌道維持。

source.title: OCO launch press kit (NASA/JPL 2009); NASA SST-SoA ch. 4
source.note: sourced: 'the 45 kilograms of propellant that it carries'; hydrazine thrusters 200-235 s (MR-111 219-229 s). estimate: 15 kg dry, 5 W heaters, cost

function.en: The standard metal box around the electronics.
function.zh-TW: 包住電子設備的標準金屬外殼

explainer.en: The standard aluminium box around the electronics. It already stops most low-energy particles; in a gentle orbit for a few years, that is enough.
explainer.zh-TW: 包住電子設備的標準鋁盒。它已經擋得住大部分低能量的粒子；在溫和的軌道上待幾年，這樣就夠了。

description.en: The usual electronics box. Every orbit's dose number in this game is quoted behind this much aluminium.
description.zh-TW: 一般的電子設備盒。遊戲中各軌道的輻射劑量都是以這個厚度為準。

source.title: Adell (NASA-JPL), Dose and Dose-Rate Effects in Micro-Electronics
source.note: sourced: mission doses are tabulated behind 100 mils (2.54 mm) of aluminium

function.en: A thicker box that protects electronics from radiation.
function.zh-TW: 比較厚的外殼，保護電子設備不受輻射

explainer.en: A thicker metal vault around the most sensitive electronics. Satellites crossing Earth's radiation belts, and probes like Juno at Jupiter, hide their computers inside vaults like this.
explainer.zh-TW: 把最敏感的電子設備關進更厚的金屬保險箱。穿過地球輻射帶的衛星，還有像朱諾號這種飛到木星的探測器，都把電腦藏在這種保險箱裡。

description.en: Thicker walls around the computer. Halves the dose in low orbit; works even better against GEO's soft electrons.
description.zh-TW: 電腦周圍加厚。低軌道劑量減半；對地球同步軌道的軟電子效果更好。

source.title: NASA NTRS: Shields-1 PLEO Dosimetry Measurements (2022)
source.note: estimate: x0.5 per doubling of Al in LEO (penetrating protons); GEO falls faster (x0.2-0.3), simplified to one factor

function.en: Heavy armour against radiation.
function.zh-TW: 很重的防輻射裝甲

explainer.en: Heavy armour for the harshest radiation. Every extra layer stops more particles, but the gains shrink while the mass keeps growing, so engineers add only as much as the orbit really needs.
explainer.zh-TW: 給輻射最強的地方用的重裝甲。每多一層就多擋一些粒子，但多擋的越來越少，重量卻一直加上去，所以工程師只加到軌道用得到的厚度。

description.en: A thick vault plus tantalum spot shields on the most sensitive chips. A quarter of the dose, for 8 kg.
description.zh-TW: 厚屏蔽艙加上最敏感晶片的鉭片局部屏蔽。劑量剩四分之一，代價 8 公斤。

source.title: NASA NTRS: Shields-1 PLEO Dosimetry Measurements (2022)
source.note: estimate: two doublings of shielding = x0.25

function.en: Finds fires on the ground, day or night.
function.zh-TW: 找出地面上的火點，白天晚上都可以

explainer.en: A flame is far hotter than the ground around it, and hot things shine brightest in mid-wave infrared, around four microns. This camera looks only in that band, so even a small fire stands out. Germany's FireBIRD satellites used the same idea to spot wildfires from orbit.
explainer.zh-TW: 火焰比周圍的地面熱得多，而高溫的東西在中波紅外線、大約四微米的地方最亮。這台相機只看這個波段，小小的火點在畫面上也很明顯。德國的 FireBIRD 衛星就是用這個原理從太空找野火。

description.en: A mid-wave infrared camera tuned near 4 microns, where an 800 K flame shines brightest. Coarse pixels, little data, but it spots fires a normal camera cannot see.
description.zh-TW: 調在 4 微米附近的中波紅外線相機，正是 800 K 火焰最亮的波段。像素粗、資料量小，但看得到一般相機看不出來的火點。

source.title: eoPortal: BIROS (Bi-spectral InfraRed Optical System, DLR FireBIRD); Frauenberger et al., The DLR FireBIRD mission (2017)
source.note: sourced: FireBIRD hot-spot recognition camera, MWIR 3.4-4.2 um and LWIR 8.5-9.3 um channels, ~370 m ground pixels from ~515 km SSO; Wien's law puts an 800 K flame's peak at 3.6 um. derived: ~500 m at 700 km (370 x 700/515). estimate: 6 kg, 18 W, 5 GB/day, cost, x0.6 detection of new small fires

function.en: Stores a little power for Earth's shadow.
function.zh-TW: 儲存一點電力，給衛星進到地球影子裡時用

explainer.en: A palm-sized pack of rechargeable lithium-ion cells, the kind used in CubeSats. It is plenty for a tiny CubeSat; but every time the spacecraft passes behind Earth, everything runs on this little pack until the Sun comes back, and a microsatellite with a real payload empties it fast.
explainer.zh-TW: 巴掌大的鋰電池組，立方衛星常用的那種。小立方衛星用很夠；但衛星每次繞到地球背後，所有東西都只能靠這一小包電撐到太陽出來，帶著完整酬載的微衛星很快就會用光。

description.en: A four-cell CubeSat pack. Fine for a CubeSat, but a microsatellite with a real payload drains it too deep even in the dawn-dusk orbit's 19-minute eclipse season, and a 35-minute shadow runs it flat.
description.zh-TW: 四顆電芯的立方衛星電池組。立方衛星用剛好，但帶著完整酬載的微衛星，就算在晨昏軌道 19 分鐘的地影季也會放電太深；進 35 分鐘的地影就撐不住。

source.title: GomSpace NanoPower BP4 datasheet (Rev 3.1, 2023)
source.note: sourced: 43 Wh nominal (four 3,000 mAh cells, 2P-2S or 1P-4S), 258 g. estimate: flight-ready cost

function.en: Measures Earth's magnetic field around the spacecraft.
function.zh-TW: 量測衛星周圍的地球磁場

explainer.en: A small sensor on a boom that feels the strength and direction of the magnetic field, the same field that turns a compass needle. Scientists map the field to study Earth's core and the space around our planet. It takes no pictures at all.
explainer.zh-TW: 裝在支桿上的小感測器，量磁場的強度和方向，就是讓指南針轉動的那個磁場。科學家用它研究地球的核心和周圍的太空環境。它不會拍照。

description.en: Tiny, cheap and frugal, and the data are real science, but they are about the magnetic field, not the ground. Almost no value for imaging, carbon or fire missions.
description.zh-TW: 又小又便宜又省電，資料也有科學價值，但量的是磁場，不是地面。對拍照、碳觀測和野火任務幾乎沒幫助。

source.title: Wikipedia: Magnetometer (fluxgate magnetometers in spacecraft)
source.note: estimate: typical CubeSat fluxgate (0.1-0.5 kg, under 1 W, a few kbit/s), cost

function.en: Spots flashes of lightning, day or night.
function.zh-TW: 日夜都能看到閃電的閃光

explainer.en: A fast camera that stares at the clouds and records every brief flash of lightning, even against bright daytime clouds. Weather scientists use it to understand storms. Lightning can start wildfires, but this sensor sees the flash, not the fire that follows.
explainer.zh-TW: 一台很快的相機，盯著雲層記錄每一道短暫的閃電，連白天明亮的雲上也看得到。氣象學家用它研究暴風雨。閃電可能引發野火，但這台儀器看到的是閃光，不是之後燒起來的火。

description.en: A LIS-class storm sensor: catches lightning flashes over 8 km cells from 700 km, day and night. It cannot detect a fire on the ground.
description.zh-TW: LIS 等級的雷暴感測器：從 700 公里高以 8 公里的格子日夜捕捉閃電。看不到地面上的火。

source.title: WMO OSCAR: Instrument LIS (TRMM); NASA Earthdata: LIS
source.note: sourced: LIS 21 kg, 33 W, 6 kbit/s, 128 x 128 CCD, ~4 km at nadir from TRMM's 350 km, total lightning day and night. derived: 8 km at 700 km (4 x 700/350), 0.07 GB/day = 6 kbit/s x 86,400 s. estimate: cost

function.en: Fires laser pulses at the surface to measure its height.
function.zh-TW: 向地表發射雷射脈衝，量出地面的高度

explainer.en: It times how long a laser pulse takes to bounce back from the surface, which gives the height of the ground below. The Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter used one to build the best topographic map of the Moon, working in the dark as well as in sunlight. Around Earth it mostly measures ice sheets, not what is on the ground.
explainer.zh-TW: 它計算雷射脈衝從地表彈回來要多久，就知道底下地面的高度。月球勘測軌道飛行器用它做出最精確的月球地形圖，在黑暗中也能量。繞地球時它主要用來量冰層，看不到地面上有什麼。

description.en: A LOLA-class altimeter. Excellent for mapping the Moon's terrain, day or night; weak for most Earth missions and blind to fires and CO2.
description.zh-TW: LOLA 等級的測高儀。畫月球地形很好用，白天晚上都能量；對大多數地球任務幫助不大，也看不到火和二氧化碳。

source.title: NASA GSFC: Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA); Smith et al., The Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter Investigation on the LRO Mission, Space Sci. Rev. 150 (2010)
source.note: sourced: LOLA instrument 12.6 kg, 34 W, 5 m laser spots from the 50 km mapping orbit. estimate: data volume, cost

name.zh-TW: 地面用矽晶太陽能翼（1.5 m²）

function.en: Fold-out solar wings made with rooftop-style silicon cells.
function.zh-TW: 用屋頂那種矽晶電池做的展開式太陽能翼

explainer.en: The same kind of silicon cells as on a house roof, mounted on fold-out wings. They are cheap and the wings are big, but each square of silicon turns less sunlight into electricity than the multi-layer cells made for space, and the thick glass that protects them is heavy.
explainer.zh-TW: 和住家屋頂一樣的矽晶電池，裝在展開式的翼板上。便宜，翼板也大，但同樣大小的矽晶電池，能把陽光變成電的比例比太空用的多層電池低，保護它的厚玻璃也很重。

description.en: Bigger than the S-2 wings on paper, but silicon cells deliver about 60 % of the power per m² of space-grade triple-junction cells, and the cover glass adds mass.
description.zh-TW: 面積比 S-2 大，但矽晶電池每平方公尺的發電量只有太空用三接面電池的六成左右，保護玻璃又增加重量。

source.title: Wikipedia: Multi-junction solar cell (space vs terrestrial efficiency)
source.note: derived: 0.6 = ~18-20 % silicon / ~30 % space triple-junction. estimate: mass (cover glass), cost

function.en: Stores a little energy and releases it very fast.
function.zh-TW: 存一點點電，可以瞬間放出來

explainer.en: A supercapacitor stores energy as separated electric charge instead of a chemical reaction, so it can charge and discharge in seconds and survive a huge number of cycles. Satellites use them to give short bursts of power. The weakness is how little energy they hold for their weight: far too little to keep a spacecraft running through the dark part of an orbit.
explainer.zh-TW: 超級電容用分開的電荷存能量，不靠化學反應，所以幾秒內就能充放電，充放很多次也不會壞。衛星用它提供短暫的大電流。弱點是同樣重量存的能量太少：根本撐不過軌道上沒有陽光的那一段。

description.en: Survives endless cycles and delivers huge bursts, but 8 Wh cannot carry the spacecraft through an eclipse. It cannot replace a battery.
description.zh-TW: 充放再多次也不會壞、瞬間電流很大，但 8 Wh 撐不過地影。不能拿來代替電池。

source.title: Wikipedia: Supercapacitor (energy density)
source.note: derived: ~7 Wh/kg packaged (cells 5-10 Wh/kg). estimate: cost

function.en: Beams data to the ground with a laser instead of radio.
function.zh-TW: 用雷射代替無線電把資料傳回地面

explainer.en: Light can carry far more data than radio, so a tiny laser terminal can beat the fastest radio by a wide margin. The catch is the weather and the ground: clouds block the beam, and only a handful of special optical ground stations can catch it. On a cloudy day, the fastest link in the world sends nothing at all.
explainer.zh-TW: 光能攜帶的資料比無線電多很多，所以小小的雷射終端，速度就能遠遠超過最快的無線電。問題在天氣和地面：雲會擋住光束，而且全世界只有少數幾座特殊的光學地面站接得到。陰天的時候，世界上最快的連線一點資料也傳不下來。

description.en: Ten times the peak rate of X-3, but it only connects in clear skies over one of a few optical stations: about 3 % of pass time. On average it moves less data than X-3 and costs more.
description.zh-TW: 峰值速率是 X-3 的十倍，但只有在少數光學地面站上空、而且天氣晴朗時才連得上，大約只有過站時間的 3%。平均傳得比 X-3 少，還更貴。

source.title: Wikipedia: Laser communication in space
source.note: estimate: 10 Gbit/s-class small terminal; 3 % availability = few optical ground stations x cloud-free probability; mass, power, cost

name.zh-TW: 消費級 AI 運算板（256 GB）

function.en: A powerful off-the-shelf computer with lots of memory.
function.zh-TW: 效能強、記憶體大的市售電腦

explainer.en: The kind of AI computer used in drones and robots: fast, cheap and full of memory. In space, though, radiation slowly damages chips that were never designed for it, and a single particle can scramble memory or crash the board. Engineers do fly boards like this, but as experiments, not as the computer the whole mission depends on.
explainer.zh-TW: 無人機和機器人用的那種 AI 電腦：快、便宜、記憶體大。可是在太空中，輻射會慢慢破壞沒有為太空設計的晶片，一顆粒子就可能讓記憶體出錯或讓整塊板子當機。工程師確實會帶這種板子上太空，但是當成實驗，不是整個任務都靠它的那台電腦。

description.en: Twice the storage of C-2 for less money, but it tolerates only 8 krad and fails often. In most orbits radiation ends the mission early.
description.zh-TW: 儲存空間是 C-2 的兩倍又比較便宜，但只耐得住 8 krad，而且容易故障。大多數軌道上，輻射會讓任務提早結束。

source.title: Wikipedia: Radiation hardening
source.note: estimate: commercial edge-AI module total-dose tolerance (~5-20 krad in tests), power, reliability, cost

function.en: Big spinning gyros that swing the spacecraft around very fast.
function.zh-TW: 大型旋轉陀螺，讓衛星快速轉向

explainer.en: A control moment gyro tilts a fast-spinning wheel to produce a strong twist, far stronger than a reaction wheel. The International Space Station and agile imaging satellites use them to turn quickly from target to target. For a small satellite that only needs to point steadily, they are heavy, hungry and more than it will ever use.
explainer.zh-TW: 控制力矩陀螺把高速旋轉的輪子傾斜，產生很大的扭力，比反應輪強很多。國際太空站和需要快速換目標的影像衛星都用它。對只需要穩穩指向的小衛星來說，它太重、太耗電，能力也遠超過需要。

description.en: Points no better than G-3 but weighs and draws far more, and costs twice as much. Agility the mission does not need.
description.zh-TW: 指向精度和 G-3 一樣，但重很多、耗電很多，價錢是兩倍。這個任務用不到這麼靈活。

source.title: Wikipedia: Control moment gyroscope
source.note: estimate: small-satellite CMG cluster mass, power, cost; pointing set equal to G-3

function.en: Electric thruster: tiny push, very little fuel, lots of electricity.
function.zh-TW: 電力推進：推力很小、燃料很少、但很耗電

explainer.en: An ion thruster uses electricity to fling charged atoms out the back at enormous speed, so a little propellant goes a very long way. Missions like Dawn crossed the asteroid belt this way. The price is power: while it runs it needs as much electricity as several instruments, and its push is gentler than a sheet of paper resting on your hand.
explainer.zh-TW: 離子推進器用電把帶電的原子以極高速度往後噴，所以一點點推進劑就能用很久。黎明號就是這樣飛過小行星帶的。代價是電力：運轉時要的電相當於好幾台儀器，推力卻比一張紙放在手上還輕。

description.en: Ten times the efficiency of chemical thrusters, so 1.5 kg of iodine lasts years, but it draws 75 W continuously. Without a much bigger solar array, the power budget breaks.
description.zh-TW: 效率是化學推進的十倍，1.5 kg 的碘就能用好幾年，但會持續耗電 75 W。沒有大很多的太陽能板，電力就不夠。

source.title: Busek BIT-3 RF ion thruster
source.note: sourced: iodine RF ion thruster, Isp up to 2,150 s (game 2,100), 56-75 W system input, 1.40 kg dry with gimbal; up to 2.39 km/s for a 14 kg CubeSat. derived: 1.5 kg iodine = 14 x (1 - exp(-2,390 / (2,150 x 9.81))). estimate: cost

function.en: Heavy lead plates around the electronics.
function.zh-TW: 在電子設備周圍加上厚重的鉛板

explainer.en: On Earth, lead is the classic radiation shield for X-rays at the dentist. In space it works worse than you would expect: when fast electrons slam into heavy lead atoms they give off new X-rays inside the box, and lead is so dense that every bit of protection costs a lot of mass. Spacecraft designers prefer aluminium, or a thin layer of a heavy metal backed by aluminium.
explainer.zh-TW: 在地面上，鉛是擋 X 光的經典材料，牙醫照 X 光就用它。到了太空效果反而變差：高速電子撞上沉重的鉛原子，會在盒子裡產生新的 X 光；而且鉛密度太高，每多一點保護就多很多重量。太空船設計師比較喜歡用鋁，或是薄薄一層重金屬再加上鋁。

description.en: Four times the mass of the R-2 vault and blocks less: secondary X-rays (bremsstrahlung) from trapped electrons eat into the gain.
description.zh-TW: 重量是 R-2 的四倍，擋得反而比較少：被困電子撞擊產生的二次 X 光（制動輻射）抵消了效果。

source.title: Wikipedia: Bremsstrahlung
source.note: estimate: x0.6 dose for 2 mm Pb (vs x0.5 for 3 kg of extra Al), bremsstrahlung from trapped electrons
